svg.aria-label: Diagram of Aurora MySQL delayed replication. A destructive statement runs on the source at 14:12 and applies immediately. A replica configured with a one hour delay is still at 13:12, so the statement has not reached it. The hour between them is the detection budget: notice within it and you stop replication, replay forward to just before the bad position with rds_start_replication_until, and promote. Miss it and the replica has applied the statement too. Below, two panels: the delay is a tradeoff, because a longer delay buys detection time and makes the replica staler as a failover target, so a delayed replica is not a disaster recovery replica; and delayed replication is configured only by stored procedure, not by the console, CLI or RDS API, so it is invisible to infrastructure as code and to configuration audits.
svg.title: How a delayed Aurora MySQL replica converts an hour of lag into a recovery window, and what that hour costs
svg.text: The only defence against a change that replicates correctly
A backup restores what was there. A delayed replica is a running database that has not yet been told.
Source — the statement applies the instant it runs
14:12 — DROP TABLE
now
Replica with target delay 3600 — still an hour behind
13:12 — replica is here
your detection budget — one hour
Notice in time and the recovery is three calls, not a restore: rds_stop_replication, then
rds_start_replication_until to replay up to just before the bad position, then promote. Miss it and the replica has applied it too.
The delay is a tradeoff, in both directions
Longer delay: more time to notice, staler standby.
Shorter delay: fresher standby, and the statement may
already have arrived before anyone looked.
So this is not your DR replica. Build a separate one.
Configured by stored procedure only
You can't configure delayed replication with the console,
the AWS CLI, or the Amazon RDS API.
So it is absent from Terraform state and from every
configuration audit — and lost when a replica is rebuilt.
Aurora MySQL 8.4.8 and higher, in all Regions where Aurora MySQL is available. Multi-source replication shipped the same day: one cluster,
several sources, for merging shards or aggregating regional databases into one place for reporting.
